title: PowerPoint on Mac: reference an existing PowerPoint file when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: The roadmap facts, file-reference workflow, licensing background and licence-management routes are supported. The governance checklist names sharing and sensitivity-label reviews that are missing from the controls table; this is a minor completeness issue.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The default state on arrival is not explicitly stated for this option.
claims.quote: Searched: "PowerPoint" "Reference file" "default"; PowerPoint Agent Mode "Reference file" license default admin control Mac. Read roadmap, release-notes feature entry and copilot/implement/configure-copilot-admin-center; no explicit arrival default found.

claims.claim: No feature-specific Microsoft Learn page beyond the release-note entry was found.
claims.quote: Searched: "555889"; "Copilot in PowerPoint" "Agent Mode"; "PowerPoint" "Reference file". Read release-notes feature entry and search results; other results cover different agents, generic training or unrelated PowerPoint APIs.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The file-reference capability respects existing file permissions and access controls.
claims.quote: This capability respects existing file permissions and access controls.

claims.claim: Copilot in PowerPoint automatically inherits a source item's sensitivity label when creating new content based on that labelled item.
claims.quote: If you use Copilot in Word, Copilot in PowerPoint, and Copilot in Outlook to create new content based on an item that has a sensitivity label applied, the sensitivity label from the source file is automatically inherited, with the label's protection settings.

claims.claim: The automatically inherited source sensitivity label carries its protection settings.
claims.quote: the sensitivity label from the source file is automatically inherited, with the label's protection settings.

claims.claim: No change to sign-in, consent or roles is described for this capability.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot in PowerPoint" "reference" "sign-in" "consent"; "Copilot in PowerPoint" "Reference file" "admin". Read release-notes entry and Copilot admin settings; no feature-specific sign-in, consent or role change found.

claims.claim: The release-note steps describe user selection and prompting, not background or scheduled action.
claims.quote: Searched: "555889" and "Copilot in PowerPoint" "Agent Mode". Read the full Reuse content and style entry in release-notes: users select Reference file and prompt Copilot; the entry describes no scheduled or background action.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; Scope; controls[0].note
claims.claim: The overview associates the full Copilot experience in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote with the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence.
claims.quote: You **have** the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The overview describes both Basic in-app Copilot access without the add-on and Premium access with it, supporting the mixed product-level licensing model.
claims.quote: **Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic)** refers to users without the Copilot add-on license, but who have access to Copilot capabilities inside apps (for example, Word or Excel).

claims.claim: Some features available without the add-on licence are subject to fair use limits.
claims.quote: You **don't** have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license but **can** use Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote. Some features are subject to **[fair use limits]

claims.claim: The Basic PowerPoint feature list includes creating presentations from prompts or existing content, summarizing and editing presentations.
claims.quote: PowerPoint: Create presentations from prompts or existing content, summarize presentations or edit presentations (add images, apply deck-wide formatting changes)

claims.claim: The Premium experience includes everything in Basic.
claims.quote: **Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium)** is the full add-on licensed experience (some features are subject to [fair use limits](https://support.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-copilot/limits-for-features-copilot-chat)), which includes everything in Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic)

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The documentation does not explicitly allocate Reference file in Agent Mode to Basic versus Premium, and the feature release-note entry names no licence.
claims.quote: Searched: "PowerPoint" "Agent Mode" license; "Copilot" "PowerPoint" "reference" "licensing". Read release-notes, copilot-overview and copilot-license-options; generic Basic creation is listed, but no explicit allocation of this Agent Mode option was found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate price, meter or credit rate is published for this file-reference option.
claims.quote: Searched: "PowerPoint" "referencing" "meter"; PowerPoint reference existing presentation Agent Mode price meter credits licensing Basic Premium. Read release-notes, copilot-overview, copilot-license-options and usage-based-billing-overview-copilot-credits; no option-specific rate found.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses reaches the user's licence selection.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the **Users** > [Active users] ... Select the row of the user ... In the right pane, select **Licenses and Apps**. ... Expand the **Licenses** section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a licence to a user through Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least License or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: The release-note entry names no feature-specific admin setting; the documented licence assignment route is not a switch for Reference file.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot in PowerPoint" "Reference file" "admin"; "PowerPoint" "reference" "Copilot" admin settings. Read release-notes, configure-copilot-admin-center and assign-licenses-to-users; no dedicated Reference file switch found.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to review sharing permissions and sensitivity labels, but neither control is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Review sharing on decks that users are likely to reference ... review that file's permissions and sensitivity label. / The only control in the table is the Copilot licence
claims.fix: The checklist steps 'Review sharing on decks that users are likely to reference' and 'review that file's permissions and sensitivity label' have no corresponding controls-table rows. Remove these control-review instructions from the checklist to resolve the mismatch without adding unverified rows.
